title: ShopView Accounts lists one row per category under Cost of Parts
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The QuickBooks page opens.

Step 2:

  • Directly under Cost of Parts and above Cost of Goods (tax), the header "Internal work orders" shows a row named General Internal.
  • Under the header "No Charge work orders" rows show for Warranty, Goodwill and Comeback.
  • Each category row carries the green QuickBooks mark.
  • Under the rows a note reads "Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders are credited to the income account of your Shop supplies item in Products And Services; nothing to map here."
  • General Internal's row carries a "Default" badge.
  • Under each header the rows follow the name order: Comeback, Goodwill, Warranty.
  • The other ShopView Accounts rows keep their place and grouping; none moved under "Other".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11762 (Story 5, QuickBooks Online account mapping), story SV-11767 (Story 10, Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders)

  • S5-R1: “Integrations > QuickBooks, ShopView Accounts, shows one row per category directly under Cost of Parts (above Cost of Goods (tax)), grouped under the headers "Internal work orders" and "No Charge work orders", each row named after its category and carrying the QuickBooks mark. A category the shop adds appears as a new empty row; an archived category keeps its row, greyed, with its mapping, and the row can still be remapped (a reopened work order still posts to its archived category, S12-E8). Under the rows a note reads "Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders are credited to the income account of your Shop supplies item in Products And Services; nothing to map here." Nothing is created in QuickBooks: the picker lists the location's existing expense accounts.”
  • S10-R5: “No new mapping row in either integration: QuickBooks credits the income account of the existing "Shop supplies" item (Products And Services) (Story 5, S5-R1 note); AccountingHub uses its existing "Shop supplies expense" row (Story 6).”
  • Terminology: “Category expense account → the expense account mapped to a category per location: one ShopView Accounts row per category in QuickBooks (S5-R1), one Account Mappings row per category in AccountingHub (S6-R1). Replaces the two fixed rows Internal Work Orders Expense and Customer No-Charge Expense of v0.17.”
  • Feature Overview: “Accounting is one expense account per category. In QuickBooks the accountant maps each category once per location, on the category itself or on the ShopView Accounts page, where the categories show as one row each under Cost of Parts; an empty row posts to ShopView Review as every unmapped row does today, with no fallback to another row. In AccountingHub, Account Mappings holds one row per category, automatically mapped for the starting categories (General Internal to 6500 Vehicle Expenses; Warranty and Goodwill to the existing 6430 Warranty & Goodwill Expense; Comeback to 6440 Comeback Expense). The rollout migration and new-customer setup reuse suitable accounts, create missing required accounts, preserve valid existing mappings and resolve number conflicts with an available number, so all starting mappings are ready before the first job posts (S6-R2); a category the shop adds gets an empty row that holds the event until it is mapped; an archived category keeps its row. The shop supplies credit is unchanged (Story 10). At Close of a whole internal or no-charge work order the parts cost debits the category's account and the credit stays on today's inventory account by part category and stock location. On a billable work order with a no-charge line, that line's parts cost posts to the category's account when the invoice is created; the rest of the work order posts as today.”
  • Key Decisions: “One expense account per category, mapped per location in QuickBooks (as every ShopView Accounts row is) and per organization in AccountingHub (as every Account Mappings row is), with the starting categories mapped automatically in the hub (S6-R2).”

From: "Internal Work Orders technical implementation plan", 2026-10-28, last updated 2026-11-10 (revision 5, built on PRD v1.0), sources/TECH-PLAN-Internal-Work-Orders-upload-2026-11-12.md, read 12 Nov 2026

  • Tech plan line 3266 (TP-421): “on the default Internal category”
